exec_summary: Eoin, there is a clear and credible commercial foundation here, with plain-language positioning, a strong client logo set and a genuinely well-designed lead-generation tool in the NetSuite pricing calculator. The most significant gaps sit in how the full breadth and sequencing of your services are presented commercially: the website lists seven service lines but does not show a buyer how they connect, what order they follow or what a full engagement looks like from start to finish. Your target customer and the geographies you serve are not stated anywhere on the site, which means buyers who match your ideal profile have to draw their own conclusions. The ERP and AI Transformation Community you have founded is one of the most commercially interesting findings in this research and represents a direct, recurring route to your ideal buyers that does not yet appear to be used as a structured business development channel.

focus.h4: Build a visible path from first engagement to full relationship
focus.p: Your website lists seven services but does not show how they connect or what the natural progression from one to the next looks like. Buyers who arrive looking for a point solution cannot currently see what else is available or why they should stay. Making that journey explicit in your collateral, on your website and in your sales conversations directly addresses the obstacle you have described.

focus.h4: Make your target customer and geography unmistakably clear
focus.p: The website does not name the types of companies you work best with, the stage of growth at which you add most value or the geographies you serve. Your client logos suggest a clear pattern of scale-up technology businesses, but that pattern is never stated. Buyers who match your ideal profile should be able to see themselves immediately when they land on your website.

focus.h4: Activate the ERP and AI Transformation Community as a commercial channel
focus.p: You have founded a networking community of ERP professionals, which represents a direct and recurring route to your ideal buyers. There is no visible evidence that this community is being used systematically to generate pipeline or showcase your expertise. Turning it into a structured commercial channel with content, events and clear next steps could be one of the highest-return investments you make.

icp_data.title: Customer Clarity
icp_data.body1: Client logos signal a clear pattern,
icp_data.body2: but target profile is never stated
icp_data.q: Is it clear who your ideal customers are from your online presence?
icp_data.h4: A recognisable client base that is never described
p: Your website homepage describes you as former finance directors who provide solutions encompassing the data and processes central to your business operations. This positions the business clearly in terms of who you are, but it does not explicitly define who you sell to. The types of companies you work with, the sectors you target, the stage of growth most relevant to your offer and the geographies you serve are not stated anywhere on the homepage or the services pages.

The client logo section on the homepage and about page provides meaningful indirect evidence. Logos for FeedzAI, Pleo, Klipboard, Exclaimer, Cyncly and WiredScore are visible. These are recognisably growth-stage technology and SaaS businesses, most of which have raised venture funding and operate internationally. This suggests a clear pattern in the customers you actually win, but that pattern is never articulated anywhere on the site. A visitor who matched your ideal profile would need to draw their own conclusions rather than being told directly.

The services page describes triggers such as inefficient processes making it difficult for your finance team to keep up with your businesses fast paced growth and operating across numerous currency zones. These phrases do speak to a recognisable type of business but remain general rather than specific. The NetSuite pricing calculator asks users to select a turnover range and country of operations, with the UK presented as a currency reference, which suggests a primary focus on the UK market. However, this is not confirmed or stated elsewhere on the site. Information on a LinkedIn company page for Coras Consulting was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

icp_data.title: Problem Understanding
icp_data.body1: Pain points named at service level,
icp_data.body2: but not connected to business outcomes
icp_data.q: Do you understand deeply the business challenges your customers are trying to solve?
icp_data.h4: Pain points acknowledged but not escalated to business consequence
p: The services page on your website addresses recognisable pain points. The selection framework section asks whether inefficient processes are making it difficult for your finance team to keep up with your businesses fast paced growth, whether the business operates across numerous currency zones and whether the client has lost faith in their month end consolidation process. These are credible, specific questions that reflect genuine problems faced by finance teams in scaling businesses.

The NetSuite optimisation page goes further, noting that clients have gone with a rapid implementation and that their business processes have not been fully considered. This is a specific and recognisable problem in the market, and stating it shows familiarity with how implementations typically fail. The blog post on financial reporting in NetSuite demonstrates hands-on knowledge of the day-to-day frustrations finance users encounter after go-live, citing the manual steps required to produce monthly management reports as the biggest complaint heard from clients.

However, the website does not connect these individual pain points to wider business outcomes. There is no content that explains what happens to a business if these problems go unresolved — the commercial risk, the cost, the competitive impact. The challenges are acknowledged but not escalated to the level of business consequence that would make a senior buyer feel urgency. The about page focuses on how Coras Consulting delivers rather than on what the buyer stands to lose or gain.

icp_data.title: Team Alignment
icp_data.q: Are your sales and marketing teams aligned around the same customer?
icp_data.h4: Limited LinkedIn evidence but directionally consistent
p: One LinkedIn post attributed to you is visible in the research data. In it, you describe a trip to London and reference the founding of a networking group called the ERP and AI Transformation Community, which you describe as being for ERP professionals. This is broadly consistent with the ERP focus on the website. The post signals an intent to build a community around the target market, which is relevant and directionally aligned with the commercial proposition.

However, the research data available does not include your full LinkedIn profile or a pattern of posts across multiple themes. It is not possible from the available evidence to assess whether your LinkedIn activity consistently targets the same customer segments that the website addresses, or whether your content regularly covers the topics that your services address. Information on a LinkedIn company page for Coras Consulting was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

As a sole-director business with one additional consultant, the concept of sales and marketing team alignment applies differently here than in a larger organisation. What can be said is that the one piece of LinkedIn activity found is consistent with the commercial direction of the website, and the founding of the ERP and AI Transformation Community suggests a deliberate effort to build presence in the target market.

icp_data.title: Commercial Credibility
icp_data.q: Do you hire commercial people who can build credibility with your buyers?
icp_data.h4: A background that closely matches the target buyer
p: Your about page describes you as a chartered accountant and former finance director with ten years of ERP functional experience and PRINCE2 project management certification. This is a directly relevant and credible background for selling into finance directors and finance teams at scaling technology businesses. The combination of finance leadership experience and technical ERP delivery capability is unusual and commercially valuable for the buyer profile you are pursuing.

Benjamin Langley is described as a NetSuite systems expert with experience across more than thirty successful implementations, with particular expertise in manufacturing and workforce planning. This is a strong technical credential for a consultant working on complex NetSuite deployments.

The WiredScore case study on the about page references a successful implementation from QuickBooks to NetSuite delivered within five months, including data migration and go-live. The client logos on the homepage, including FeedzAI, Pleo, Klipboard, Exclaimer and Cyncly, suggest that buyers in the target market have already assessed the credibility of the team and engaged. Your background as a former finance director means you are selling peer-to-peer into the finance leadership roles you are targeting, which is a significant credibility advantage.

icp_data.title: Geographic Targeting
icp_data.body2: on any part of the website
icp_data.q: Do you have a targeted approach for each market and geography you sell into?
icp_data.h4: No geographic targeting visible anywhere on the site
p: The website does not name any specific geographies that Coras Consulting operates in or targets. There is no mention of the UK, Ireland or any other market on the homepage, the services pages or the about page. The NetSuite pricing calculator references pound sterling as the currency option for turnover ranges, which implies a UK focus, but this is not stated explicitly and is the only geographic signal present across the site.

No office locations are listed anywhere on the website. The about page does not mention where the business is based or where it delivers work. There is no content produced for or tailored to specific regional markets. There are no market-specific case studies, no regional references in blog content and no mention of attendance at events or conferences in particular geographies.

The LinkedIn post available in the research mentions travel to London, which suggests activity in the UK market, but this is a single data point and does not constitute a stated or structured market approach. Information on a LinkedIn company page with geographic targeting was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

prod_data.title: Proposition Clarity
prod_data.q: Can your proposition be quickly and easily understood?
prod_data.h4: A clear proposition that stops short of showing the full picture
p: The homepage headline reads Complex Made Simple and the opening description states that you are former finance directors who provide solutions encompassing the data and processes central to your business operations, with a mission to make your job easier. This is written in plain language and communicates the core offer in under thirty seconds. The phrase former finance directors establishes credibility immediately and the phrase make your job easier is direct and customer-facing rather than technical in tone.

The seven service lines listed on the homepage are labelled in plain English and each links to a dedicated page. Each service page opens with a customer-facing question or problem statement rather than a description of the service itself, which keeps the language oriented towards the buyer. The blog post on financial reporting in NetSuite is written in accessible, practical language with no unnecessary technical complexity. The NetSuite pricing calculator is similarly self-explanatory.

The proposition is clear and understandable. The main limitation is that the seven services are listed as discrete items without a clear explanation of how they relate to each other or what a full engagement looks like.

prod_data.title: Problem Definition
prod_data.body1: Pain points named on service pages,
prod_data.q: Do your products solve clearly defined customer problems?
prod_data.h4: Problems identified but not connected to their full business cost
p: The services page uses customer-facing problem statements to open each service description. For the selection framework, it asks whether inefficient processes are making it difficult for the finance team to keep up with growth, whether the business operates across multiple currency zones and whether the client has lost faith in their month-end consolidation process. These are recognisable, specific problems for the target buyer.

The NetSuite optimisation service description acknowledges a common post-implementation failure mode: that clients have gone live with a rapid implementation without fully considering business processes. This shows familiarity with a real and recurring problem in the market. The financial reporting blog post details specific limitations of NetSuite reporting post-go-live and offers practical solutions, grounding the content in a genuine day-to-day problem for finance users.

However, none of the service descriptions move from problem identification to commercial consequence. They describe the problem at a surface level but do not explain what it costs the business in time, money or risk to leave it unresolved. The WiredScore case study demonstrates a successful outcome but does not describe the business impact of that outcome or what would have happened without the engagement. The link between problem, solution and measurable business result is not yet fully made on the website.

prod_data.title: Entry Point
prod_data.q: Is there a clear jumping off point for new customers?
prod_data.h4: A well-designed entry point in the pricing calculator
p: The NetSuite pricing calculator is a strong and specific entry point for prospective clients. It is gated by name, business name, email address and phone number, and it walks a user through a structured set of questions about their business, including turnover range, country of operations, number of finance staff, modules required and number of user licences. This is a meaningful and genuinely useful tool for a buyer considering NetSuite, and it captures lead contact details in exchange for a personalised cost estimate.

This is an unusually well-considered lead-generation mechanism for a consultancy of this size. It requires the buyer to invest a small amount of time and effort, which increases the quality of the lead, and it provides something of genuine practical value in return.

The services pages each contain a See More link and an implied invitation to make contact, and the about page links to client case studies. However, beyond the pricing calculator, there is no other formal low-barrier entry engagement described, no discovery call offer, no sample deliverable and no clearly described initial engagement package. The pricing calculator stands as the single strongest entry point.

prod_data.title: Upsell Visibility
prod_data.q: Do you have clear upsell and cross-sell opportunities within your offering?
prod_data.h4: A logical service journey that is never made visible to the buyer
p: Seven distinct service lines are listed on the website: Selection Framework, Implementation, Project Management, Data Migration, Integrations, NetSuite Optimisation and Oracle Optimisation. These represent a logical end-to-end journey through an ERP lifecycle, from selecting a system to implementing it, migrating data and then optimising it post-go-live.

However, nowhere on the website is this progression made explicit to a buyer. There is no map of how a client might move from one service to another. There are no packages, no bundled offerings, no descriptions of what a full engagement looks like and no indication of what typically comes after an initial piece of work. A buyer who engages for a single service has no visible commercial prompt to consider the next step.

This is directly relevant to the obstacle you have described: winning a point-solution engagement and then struggling to stay in with the client to sell more. The upsell and cross-sell path is not commercially visible. Information on whether this journey is described in the uploaded deck was not available, as the file did not extract successfully.

prod_data.title: Pricing Alignment
prod_data.q: Is your pricing aligned to the value you create?
prod_data.h4: Pricing absent from services; calculator addresses licence cost only
p: No pricing is listed anywhere on the website for any of the seven service lines. This is common in consulting, where projects vary in scope, but it means that a buyer has no reference point for the investment involved before reaching out.

The NetSuite pricing calculator is a partial exception. It provides a personalised estimate of NetSuite licence costs based on the buyer's specific configuration. This is genuinely useful and creates a concrete, quantified starting point for a conversation. However, it addresses the cost of the NetSuite licence itself rather than the cost of Coras Consulting's services, so it does not close the pricing gap for the consultancy work.

The services descriptions speak to value in general terms, including reducing risk, delivering on time and within budget and making the client's job easier, but they do not quantify that value or explain what the cost of inaction or a poor implementation would be. The WiredScore case study mentions a five-month go-live timeline as an outcome but does not attach a cost or commercial value to it.

sales_data.title: Buying Journey
sales_data.q: Does your sales process have a clear beginning, middle and end?
sales_data.h4: No visible buying journey for a prospective client to follow
p: No buying process is described anywhere on the website. A prospective client visiting coras-consulting.com cannot find any explanation of what happens after they make contact, how a project is scoped, what stages they would go through or what a typical engagement looks like from start to finish. The services pages describe what each service involves in general terms but do not set out the steps a buyer would take to engage.

The implementation service page does describe a project delivery sequence, starting from system design through configuration, testing, data migration, cutover and go-live, but this describes the delivery process for an implementation project and not the buying journey a new client would experience before and during the decision to engage.

The NetSuite pricing calculator creates an entry point and captures lead details, but there is no description of what happens after a buyer submits the calculator. A prospective client who completes the calculator has no visibility of the next step. Information on whether the uploaded deck describes a buying journey was not available, as the file did not extract successfully.

sales_data.title: Buyer-Centred Design
sales_data.q: Is your sales process designed around how customers buy rather than how you prefer to sell?
sales_data.h4: Buyer orientation evident in content but not in the full journey
p: The form indicates that Coras Consulting has developed discovery scripts, cold calling scripts and message sequences. This suggests a structured approach to the early stages of a sales conversation that is oriented around uncovering the buyer's situation and needs, which is consistent with how a finance director or CFO at a scaling technology business would expect a consultancy conversation to begin.

The services page uses customer-facing problem statements to open each service description, which reflects an orientation towards the buyer's starting point rather than a description of the service from the supplier's perspective. The pricing calculator similarly begins from the buyer's point of view, asking questions about their business before providing an output.

However, there is no visible buying journey, no description of a discovery process available to a prospect before they engage and no content that walks a buyer through how decisions are typically made in this space. Buyers considering an ERP implementation are making a significant, high-risk investment decision. The public-facing commercial presence does not yet fully reflect the care with which such a buyer would need to be taken through the process.

sales_data.title: Process Adoption
sales_data.q: Is your team aligned around the same sales process?
sales_data.h4: Internally defined process confirmed as actively used
p: The form answer states clearly that you have put together a robust sales process, discovery scripts, cold calling scripts and message sequences which are well defined and used. This is a direct and specific affirmative answer to whether the sales process is actively used by the team.

Given that the business currently operates with two people, a director and a consultant, the scope of team alignment is narrow, but the self-reported answer is unambiguous. The form also rates internal buying process clarity at 7 out of 10, which is consistent with a business that has defined its process but acknowledges room for improvement.

Information on whether this alignment is visible externally through LinkedIn activity or public-facing content was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

sales_data.title: Process Repeatability
sales_data.q: Is your sales process repeatable across the business?
sales_data.h4: Process exists but self-assessed as not yet fully established
p: The form reports a sales process establishment score of 4 out of 10. This self-assessment is notable and suggests that while discovery scripts and message sequences exist and are used, the overall sales process is not yet considered well-established by the person running it.

The business currently operates with two people, which limits the scope of repeatability as a concern. However, you have described being brought in by recruiters as a point solution, which suggests that a significant portion of new business comes through an inbound or referred channel rather than through the proactive outbound process that the scripts and sequences are designed to support. Whether the defined process is consistently applied across both channels is not clear from the available evidence.

The combination of a 4 out of 10 self-rating on process establishment and the obstacle described, struggling to retain and expand client relationships beyond an initial engagement, suggests that the process, while defined in its early stages, is not yet fully embedded as a repeatable commercial engine.

sales_data.title: Selling Methodology
sales_data.q: Do you use a particular selling system or methodology?
sales_data.h4: Sandler named and confirmed as the internal selling methodology
p: The form answer names Sandler as the selling methodology used by the business. Sandler is a recognised and widely used selling system with a structured approach to qualification, pain uncovering and deal progression. It is directly relevant to the type of complex, consultative sales that ERP advisory engagements involve.

The form also confirms that discovery scripts, cold calling scripts and message sequences are in place and used, which is consistent with the disciplined qualification approach that Sandler emphasises.

coll_data.title: Public Collateral
coll_data.q: How targeted towards your ideal customer is your publicly available collateral?
coll_data.h4: Relevant content that stops short of full buyer targeting
p: The services pages on your website use customer-facing problem statements that speak to recognisable challenges for finance leaders in scaling businesses, including lost faith in month-end consolidation, inefficient processes and rapid implementations that did not fully consider business processes. This language is relevant to the buyer and is written from their perspective rather than a purely technical standpoint.

The financial reporting blog post is a useful piece of practical content that addresses a specific, common problem for finance users after a NetSuite go-live. It is written at the right level for a finance director or controller who is managing a post-implementation system. The WiredScore case study on the about page provides a concrete example of a successful engagement, including the challenge context and a five-month go-live timeline. However, the case study does not describe the business outcome achieved by WiredScore as a result of the implementation, which limits its persuasive force.

The client logos, including FeedzAI, Pleo, Klipboard, Exclaimer, Cyncly and WiredScore, are recognisable SaaS and technology brands that will resonate with buyers in the same market. Their presence acts as implicit social proof, even without detailed case studies attached to each. The website does not contain sector-specific content, buyer persona-specific journeys or content targeted at different stages of the buyer's decision process.

coll_data.title: Pitch Deck
coll_data.q: How targeted towards your ideal customer is the pitch deck or collateral you shared directly with us?
coll_data.h4: Uploaded deck could not be assessed; scored on public materials
p: The file Coras Consulting Solution Playback Deck was uploaded by you as part of this submission. The text content of the file was not successfully extracted during processing, so its specific content, structure, messaging and targeting cannot be assessed directly.

In the absence of extractable content from the deck, this answer is scored based on the publicly available collateral assessed elsewhere in this report. The publicly available materials are partially targeted towards the ideal customer, with recognisable problem statements and relevant social proof, but without explicit buyer persona targeting, geographic specificity or a clear path through the buying journey.

Information on whether the deck addresses these gaps was not available from the research data provided. Macanta's reviewers may wish to manually review the uploaded deck and amend this answer before the report is shared.

coll_data.title: Revenue Support
coll_data.body2: service pages lack calls to action
coll_data.q: Does every asset support revenue generation rather than simply provide information?
coll_data.h4: One strong conversion asset; other pages lack clear next steps
p: The NetSuite pricing calculator is the strongest revenue-supporting asset on the site. It requires a buyer to submit contact details before receiving an output, and it positions Coras Consulting directly in the context of a buying decision. A prospective client using it is actively considering a NetSuite investment. This is a clear, well-designed conversion mechanism.

The services pages contain See More links that expand descriptions, and the about page references case studies. However, no service page contains a clear call to action that moves a buyer to the next step. There is no book a discovery call, talk to us or equivalent prompt at the conclusion of a service description. A buyer who has read a service page and is interested has no explicit next step to follow.

The financial reporting blog post is informative and relevant but does not contain a call to action at the end. A reader who finds the post useful has no prompted path to making contact or learning more. The WiredScore case study describes an outcome but does not invite the reader to start a conversation about their own situation.

coll_data.title: Market Localisation
coll_data.q: How localised is your collateral towards your target markets?
coll_data.h4: No geographic specificity in any publicly available collateral
p: No collateral on the website names a specific geography, market or region. The services pages, blog content and case studies contain no references to the UK, Ireland or any other target market. The homepage makes no geographic claim. The about page does not state where the business is based or where it delivers work.

The NetSuite pricing calculator uses pound sterling as the currency reference for turnover ranges, which implies a UK orientation, but this is the only geographic signal in any publicly available asset. It is not stated explicitly and could be read as an oversight rather than a deliberate market positioning choice.

The WiredScore case study references a business with a global footprint, which might imply cross-border capability, but this is not drawn out or made explicit. Information on whether the uploaded deck addresses specific target markets was not available, as the file did not extract successfully.

coll_data.title: Message Consistency
coll_data.q: Is your messaging consistent across presentations, proposals and marketing materials?
coll_data.h4: Consistent internally; cross-channel picture too limited to fully assess
p: Across the publicly available assets, including the website homepage, services pages, about page and the blog post, the core themes are consistent. The framing of former finance directors who understand both systems and finance, the focus on ERP selection, implementation and optimisation and the plain-language tone are all present and coherent across the site.

The one LinkedIn post found in the research is broadly consistent in theme, referencing ERP professionals and a community built around ERP and AI transformation, though it is a single data point and cannot support a conclusion about the consistency of your LinkedIn presence overall.

The uploaded deck could not be assessed, as the file did not extract successfully. It is not possible to confirm whether the deck uses the same messaging, language and positioning as the website and other materials. Information on a LinkedIn company page was also not available from the research data.

mc_data.title: Channel Mix
mc_data.q: Are you leveraging the most appropriate channels to reach your ideal customers?
mc_data.h4: A high-value community channel that is not yet fully activated
p: The website is the primary public-facing channel and, as assessed across this report, it contains useful content, particularly the pricing calculator and the blog post, that is relevant to the target buyer.

The most significant channel asset identified in this research is the ERP and AI Transformation Community referenced in your LinkedIn post. You describe founding this networking group for ERP professionals following a trip to London. A community whose members are ERP professionals is a direct and recurring route to potential clients, referral partners and implementation recruiters. This is a potentially high-value business development channel, particularly given the obstacle you have described of being brought in as a point solution and struggling to build broader relationships with clients.

However, there is no visible evidence from the publicly available research data that this community is being used as a structured business development channel with content, events, regular touchpoints or clear next steps for members who could become clients. Information on YouTube presence, podcast appearances or other content channels for Coras Consulting was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

mc_data.title: Brand Clarity
mc_data.q: How much of a clear picture can a prospect develop of your business and your leadership before they reach out?
mc_data.h4: A reasonable starting picture on the website but limited depth elsewhere
p: A prospective buyer visiting the website can establish that the business is run by a chartered accountant and former finance director with ten years of ERP experience and PRINCE2 certification, supported by a NetSuite consultant with more than thirty implementations to his name. They can see logos of recognisable technology and SaaS clients, read one detailed case study involving WiredScore and access a blog post on a specific NetSuite topic. This provides a reasonable initial picture of the business and its credibility.
The pricing calculator gives a prospective buyer an interactive tool that demonstrates the business's understanding of how NetSuite is priced, which further establishes expertise.

However, the about page provides minimal personal depth. There is no description of the specific types of clients you work best with, no description of your background beyond professional certifications and no sense of what it is like to work with Coras Consulting beyond the single case study. The LinkedIn post found in the research adds one additional data point, your initiative in founding the ERP and AI Transformation Community, but a prospective buyer would need to find this independently. Information on the full extent of your LinkedIn profile and posting history was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

mc_data.title: Campaign Execution
mc_data.q: How well are you executing multi-channel campaigns driving clarity of message, continuity of story and purpose of the business?
mc_data.h4: No evidence of coordinated multi-channel campaign activity
p: The available research data shows a website with consistent internal messaging and one LinkedIn post attributed to you. There is no evidence of multi-channel campaign activity, no evidence of coordinated content across LinkedIn and the website, no blog posts amplified through social media, no webinars, no podcast appearances and no event presence that can be identified in the publicly available research.

The website contains one blog post with a publication date of August 2024. No other blog content is evidenced. The website lists seven services and a case study but does not show a content programme designed to attract or nurture prospective buyers at different stages of a decision journey.

Information on whether campaigns, webinars, podcast appearances or other channel activity exist but are not publicly visible was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available. Based on what is visible, the current activity level across channels is limited.

mc_data.title: Channel Engagement
mc_data.q: What level of engagement are you seeing across all of your channels?
mc_data.h4: No engagement data available from the research
p: The research data available does not include engagement metrics for the website, LinkedIn posts, blog content or any other channel. The one LinkedIn post found in the research, about the founding of the ERP and AI Transformation Community, is a single data point and does not provide a basis for assessing engagement levels across your LinkedIn activity.

No YouTube channel, podcast, webinar series or social media presence attributable to Coras Consulting was found in the research data. The blog on the website contains one published post, and no engagement data, including comments, shares or social amplification, is visible for it.
Information on engagement levels across any channel was neither provided directly through the form, nor is publicly visible from the research data available.

mc_data.title: Funnel Entry Points
mc_data.q: Are there relevant and publicly available touch points for prospects to engage with to fall into your sales funnel?
mc_data.h4: One strong funnel entry point; limited alternatives beyond it
p: The NetSuite pricing calculator is the strongest and most deliberately designed touch point on the site. It is gated by contact details, it provides genuine value to a buyer considering NetSuite and it positions Coras Consulting at the moment a buyer is actively considering an ERP investment. This is a well-considered entry point.

The website homepage and services pages are publicly accessible and contain enough information for a buyer to understand the basic offer and make contact. The about page provides team information and the WiredScore case study.

However, beyond the pricing calculator, there are no other gated assets, no newsletter sign-up, no event or webinar registration, no contact form with a clearly described next step and no calls to action at the end of service pages or the blog post. A buyer who does not use the pricing calculator has limited structured ways to enter the sales funnel without picking up the phone or sending an email directly. The ERP and AI Transformation Community referenced in your LinkedIn post could become a significant additional touch point, but there is no public-facing entry point for it visible in the research data.
